issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (and require a SealSaloon.stock attribute of type Stock), but the template repository does not provide a usable Stock implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java is empty). Instead, the template/solution include an Inventory class that implements the expected inventory API. This naming/type mismatch between 'Stock' (in the specification) and 'Inventory' (in the provided code) is structural and will confuse students about which type to use for the shared stock attribute and related static methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming and types consistent across all artifacts. Either: (a) provide a concrete Stock class implementation in the template (implementing add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) and update the solution to use Stock, or (b) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Remove or implement the empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java so students are not blocked by a missing/empty type.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (and expect a static 'Stock stock' attribute on SealSaloon), but the provided template and solution code implement this concept as a class named 'Inventory'. This naming mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) creates cognitive mapping confusion: students reading the problem will look for a 'Stock' class/file and a 'Stock' type in SealSaloon, but the codebase consistently uses 'Inventory' instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (and update all references in template and solution code to use Stock), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock' (including instructions that the static attribute is of type Inventory). Ensure the repository contains a non-empty Stock.java if the problem keeps 'Stock', or remove/replace the empty Stock.java and keep Inventory if the problem is updated.
